outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor formatting/wording (e.g., how the agent labels the results) would be nitpicks, but they are not the main problem here.

Critical issues:
1) Missing primary deliverable: The task requires reporting title + complete First release date for the first THREE dated Album entries. The agent only provided one entry (Homework) and explicitly said the next step would be to do Discovery later. This fails the stopping condition requirement to stop after recording the first three—because it never recorded three.
2) Likely wrong date source for entry #1: On the Homework release-group page (DOM state 1), there is no clearly displayed release-group-level field labeled “First release date.” The visible date (e.g., “FR 1997-01-20”) appears in a Release events table, which is per release event rather than explicitly the release-group “First release date” field the task demanded. So even the single provided date is not clearly compliant with the instruction to use the release-group page’s First release date field.

Outcome analysis: The agent did navigate correctly to the Daft Punk artist page’s Album section and opened the Homework release-group page (supported by action history and DOM). However, it did not open the release-group pages for the second and third chronological dated Album entries (Discovery and Human After All), and did not report their First release dates. Because the user’s fundamental goal is a 3-item set of title + release-group First release date, delivering only 1 item (and with questionable date provenance) would not satisfy an average user.
outcome.primary_intent: Extract, from the official Daft Punk MusicBrainz artist page, the first three dated entries shown in the standalone Album section of official release groups (skipping any undated items), open each of those three release-group pages, and report each album title plus the release-group page’s complete “First release date.” A reasonable user would not be flexible on missing any of the three entries, using the wrong section (e.g., Album+Compilation), or using per-country/per-release event dates instead of the release-group “First release date.”
